appraisal_events.evidence: la somme de ses œuvres... avait pris dans le grand public une extraordinaire puissance d'expansion; il assistait à celui de ses œuvres vers la Renommée; ses œuvres... entraînaient chaque jour jusqu'au pied de son lit des admirateurs nouveaux.
appraisal_events.explanation: Even as Bergotte's body fails, the narrator emphasizes that his literary fame and following grow dramatically, an unusual reversal in which a still-living author witnesses his own rise toward renown.

appraisal_events.evidence: je ne l'admirais plus autant... Dès lors j'admirai moins Bergotte dont la limpidité me parut de l'insuffisance.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly states that his own personal admiration for Bergotte cooled once a new, more difficult writer appeared, so that Bergotte's prized clarity came to read as mere insufficiency.

status_effects.explanation: Bergotte's public standing and literary renown rise sharply within the passage, expanding among the wider public even as his health fails.
In the narrator's own private judgment, Bergotte's stature diminishes as his once-prized clarity now reads as insufficient next to a newer, more difficult writer.

ambiguities: The narrator frames his own cooling admiration for Bergotte (E2) as a normal, recurring phenomenon of shifting literary taste ('Ce qui n'est pas en contradiction avec ce grandissement de sa renommée') rather than a definitive verdict on Bergotte's worth, so this diminishment should be read as a personal, time-bound reassessment coexisting with his rising public fame, not a retraction of it.
